solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sheep from flock west of Scottish town

indicators.note: in a down-reading sense of the grid, west means to the left, so the flock comes before the town

parts.note: a flock of animals is a herd
Wick is a town in Caithness, in the far north of Scotland

explanation.surface: A sheep's origin is traced to a flock grazing just west of a town in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'west of' places the first piece to the left of the second in an across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Herdwick is a hardy breed of sheep from the Lake District in north-west England.

clue.text: Hot, a remarkable African capital

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
rare means unusual or remarkable

explanation.surface: A traveller describes an African capital as hot and remarkable.
explanation.definitionFit: Harare is the capital city of Zimbabwe.

clue.text: Duke of Cornwall's wife, for example, went without

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so the word for went sits around the abbreviation

parts.note: ran means went, as a road or a person goes
e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Suggests a duke's wife went without something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking. In Shakespeare's King Lear the Duke of Cornwall's wife is one of Lear's daughters.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's King Lear, Lear's daughter Regan is the wife of the Duke of Cornwall.

clue.text: Partners back film

parts.note: in bridge, W and E (West and East) are partners
the stern is the back of a boat

explanation.surface: Partners decide to support a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like a verb meaning support; it is the rear of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A western is a film genre set in the American Old West, so it is a type of film.

clue.text: Body of people with crime writer detailed to tour university college

indicators.note: the body of people goes round the abbreviation for university

parts.note: a corps is an organised body of people

indicators.note: read as de-tailed, the writer's name loses its tail letter

parts.note: Agatha Christie, the detective novelist

explanation.surface: A group joins a crime novelist on a detailed tour of a university college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' is read as de-tailed, losing a last letter; 'to tour' means going round.
explanation.definitionFit: Corpus Christi is the name of a college at both Oxford and Cambridge universities.

clue.text: False report an eccentric circulates

indicators.note: the eccentric goes round, surrounding the word an placed within

parts.note: a card is an old-fashioned word for an eccentric or comic person

explanation.surface: An oddball spreads a false rumour around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circulates' means goes around, so one piece encloses the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A canard is an unfounded rumour or hoax story, borrowed from French.

clue.text: Bid a tenner at first to tantalise

indicators.note: only the opening letter of tenner is used

parts.note: to tempt is to tantalise or entice

explanation.surface: An auction bidder offers a tenner straight away to tempt the seller.
explanation.definitionFit: A bid is an attempt or effort to achieve something, as in a bid for freedom.

clue.text: Scientific study: like essay about new moon

parts.note: as means like, in the same way

indicators.note: the word for essay surrounds the rearranged letters

parts.note: to essay is to try, attempt

indicators.note: signals the letters of moon made new in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A scientific study written like a school essay about the new moon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essay' looks like a noun, but it is the verb meaning attempt; 'new' and 'about' both act on what follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomy is the science that studies stars, planets and other celestial bodies.

clue.text: Drop off short skirt to be collected by fine-looking girl

indicators.note: the skirt is gathered up inside the word for the girl

parts.note: dish is slang for an attractive person
a miniskirt, a mini

explanation.surface: A miniskirt dropped off for an attractive girl to collect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop off' suggests delivering or dozing; here it means decline. 'to be collected by' signals one piece held inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop off is to decline or decrease, as sales drop off, a sense shared with dwindle.

clue.text: Person keeping official records for hospital doctor

definitions.meaning: an official who records births, marriages and deaths
in UK hospitals a ... is a doctor in specialist training, below consultant

explanation.surface: Someone keeps official records on behalf of a hospital doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: The same title covers a keeper of public records and a grade of hospital doctor in the UK.

clue.text: A series of ups and downs as ocean wave hits vessel

definitions.text: A series of ups and downs

parts.note: a roller is a long swelling wave
a coaster is a ship trading along the coast

explanation.surface: An ocean wave strikes a ship, tossing it up and down.
explanation.definitionFit: A turbulent time with highs and lows is figuratively called a rollercoaster, after the fairground ride.

clue.text: Some come to terms over fetish?

indicators.note: turned over, so the run of letters picked out is read backwards
only some of the letters of the phrase come to terms are used, a run lying across its words

explanation.surface: Asks whether coming to terms with something counts as a fixation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks METOT from the phrase; 'over' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A fetish in the anthropological sense is an object revered as having spiritual power, like a totem.

clue.text: Poem and piece of music heard

indicators.note: signals that the musical word is spoken, giving a sound shared with a differently spelt word

parts.note: a rondo is a musical piece whose main theme keeps returning

explanation.surface: A poem paired with a piece of music, both listened to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' says the musical RONDO sounds like the poetic form.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondeau is a French verse form with a refrain, used by Villon and others.

clue.text: Satirise a politician taken in by rascal

indicators.note: the first pieces are swallowed up inside the word for rascal

parts.note: loon is an old word for a scamp or rogue
MP is Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A cartoonist mocks a politician who has been conned by a rogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in by' looks like being fooled; here it means placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To lampoon someone is to ridicule them in satirical writing or caricature.

clue.text: Diligent cousins notice changes

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are altered into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Careful relatives spot changes.
explanation.definitionFit: Being conscientious means taking great care to do one's work properly, a close synonym of diligent.

clue.text: Clear out of joint with ladder

parts.note: a cut is a joint of meat
and means together with
a ladder in stockings is also called a run

explanation.surface: Someone is told to clear out of a building site joint carrying a ladder.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut and run is to make a quick getaway, an idiom for leaving hurriedly.

clue.text: Longs to nurse poorly Greek hero

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so the longing word wraps the illness word

parts.note: to ache for something is to long for it
ill means unwell

explanation.surface: Someone yearns to care for a sick Greek hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to nurse' means to hold, so one piece cradles the other; 'Longs' is a verb here, not lengths.
explanation.definitionFit: Achilles is the warrior hero of Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: I visit in class, without exception

indicators.note: the first pieces are placed inside the word for class

parts.note: a category is a class or group
to call on someone is to visit them

explanation.surface: A school inspector announces a classroom visit, for every class with no exceptions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the first two pieces inside the word for class, just before its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something categorically means stating it absolutely, admitting no exception.

clue.text: Departs in lagoon after repairing canal craft

indicators.note: the abbreviation sits inside the rearranged letters
the letters of lagoon are mended into a new order

parts.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: A boat leaves the lagoon after being repaired, bound for the canals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after repairing' rearranges LAGOON to GONOLA; 'in' puts D inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A gondola is the flat-bottomed boat used on the canals of Venice.

clue.text: Very drunk on fewer

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
less means a smaller amount

explanation.surface: Seemingly a remark that someone is very drunk on fewer drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side of the field and the leg side are the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Legless is British slang for so drunk as to be unable to stand.

clue.text: Robber in gang, Italian

parts.note: a band is a group or gang
It is short for Italian, as in It vermouth

explanation.surface: A thief belongs to an Italian gang.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit is an armed robber, typically one of a gang attacking travellers.

clue.text: Knock public house sign, unfortunately

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: suggests something gone wrong, so the letters of sign are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone bangs into a pub sign, with bad luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' turns SIGN into INGS. In cricket a batsman's knock is an innings.
explanation.definitionFit: Knock is informal cricket slang for a batsman's innings, a spell at the crease.

clue.text: Lab gear reassembled for this subject at school

indicators.note: equipment put back together in a different way, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Laboratory equipment is put back together for a school lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: Algebra is a branch of mathematics taught in schools, so it is a school subject.

clue.text: Agent, not quite penniless

indicators.note: the word falls just short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a broker is an agent who buys and sells for others

explanation.surface: An agent who is almost out of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Broke is informal for having no money at all.

clue.text: Fat? Briefly run, slowly

indicators.note: cut short, so the word for fat loses its final letter

parts.note: lard is pig fat used in cooking
to go is to run, as a machine runs or goes

explanation.surface: A plump person is told to run only briefly and slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' trims LARD to LAR. 'Fat' wants to be LARGE; it is LARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is a musical tempo marking meaning slowly and broadly.

clue.text: Up for a big band number

definitions.meaning: keen or willing to do something
A 1939 swing hit by the Glenn Miller Orchestra

explanation.surface: Someone is keen to play a big band tune.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means willing or eager, and it is also the title of Glenn Miller's famous swing tune.

clue.text: Son not out, rotten sailor

parts.note: a batsman not out is still in, in cricket
bad, as in spoiled food

explanation.surface: A worthless son who stays home is a poor seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinbad is the legendary sailor of the Arabian Nights tales.

clue.text: Islamic emblem in curved terrace

definitions.meaning: a symbol of a waxing moon associated with Islam
a row of houses built in an arc, common in British streets such as Bath's Royal ...

explanation.surface: A symbol of Islam found on a curved row of houses.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names the moon-shaped Islamic symbol and an arc-shaped street of houses.
